newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit recovers after hitting 33-month low vs dlr.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit recovers after hitting 33-month low vs dlr.

text.p: The ringgit recovered slightly against the dollar on profit-taking by funds, after it earlier sank to a 33-month low, dealers said.
"There has been quite a bit of profit-taking but there was also good buying interest in the dollar below 2.5550," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
He noted good-sized buying demand at 2.5500/20 from local players.
The dollar/ringgit surged to 2.5700 to a dollar overnight in New York, its strongest level since October 1994, before Bank Negara intervened to cap its rise.
Dealers said speculative funds sold the ringgit down after Acting Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Monday the ringgit was still within a "reasonable range".
On Tuesday, Anwar also said that Malaysia would allow the exchange rate to be determined by market forces and that the country did not favour a high interest rate regime.
Dealers said Anwar's comments had baffled the market after Bank Negara governor Ahmad Mohamed Don said last week that interest rates would stay high to curb ringgit speculation.
The statement was also interpreted that the authorities were willing to tolerate further ringgit weakness, they said.
Dealers said given the uncertainty in the region, funds were likely to now push dollar/ringgit towards 2.6000.
At 1000 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5580/10 to a dollar. It closed at 2.5310/30 in Kuala Lumpur on Monday.
